answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with single-use proof-of-work admission: each new identity solves a fresh challenge whose sha256 digest must reach a required number of leading zero bits, and that proof is spent once. Difficulty rises whenever many joins arrive at once, so forging a thousand agents costs a thousand separate expiring hash searches. Earned rewards vest over about 25 epochs, so a fast farm cannot cash out. Reputation becomes a mirror of real work, not a fable written by a bot, and even an umber haze of doubt hangs over a name that never paid its way.
